name: Bytaria Simple Enquiry
author: bytaria

sections.description:
Bytaria Simple Enquiry is a minimal contact and quote enquiry form for WordPress.

Features:
* Shortcode-based form with name, email, phone, project location and message.
* Responsive, accessible labels and keyboard focus states.
* Email notifications with Reply-To set to the visitor’s address.
* Nonce, honeypot, time-based spam checks and basic IP-hash rate limiting.
* No file uploads, external scripts, analytics or persistent submission database.
* Configure recipient, subject, form colours, frontend language, and five optional extra fields under Settings > Simple Enquiry.
* Preserves entered form values in this browser tab for up to 15 minutes after a rejected submission; clears them on success.
* Retrieves form security tokens and submission confirmations through uncached WordPress endpoints.

Customisation

Set field labels, up to five extra fields, and hex text/button colours in Settings > Simple Enquiry. Custom field labels are shared across all languages.

Use [bytaria_enquiry_form lang=”et”] for Estonian, lang=”ar” for Arabic, lang=”zh_CN” for Simplified Chinese, lang=”zh_TW” for Traditional Chinese, or omit lang to use the selected frontend language (or the site locale when set to default). English is the fallback.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin ZIP through Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. Go to Settings > Simple Enquiry and set the recipient email address.
  4. Add a Shortcode block containing [bytaria_enquiry_form] to any page.
  5. Submit a test enquiry and verify that email arrives in the recipient inbox.

To show a privacy notice link, use:
[bytaria_enquiry_form privacy_url=”/privaatsuspoliitika/”]

To hide the project location field, use:
[bytaria_enquiry_form location=”no”]
sections.faq:
Are messages saved in WordPress?

No. Messages are sent using wp_mail() and are not stored as entries in the database. Configure reliable outbound mail delivery.

Does this prevent all spam?

No. The included measures reduce basic automated spam, but no anti-spam solution is perfect. A stronger anti-spam option may be necessary for high-traffic sites.

Does it upload attachments?

No.

Does it collect personal data?

Submitted contact details and messages are emailed to the configured recipient. Short-lived salted IP hashes are stored in transients for rate limiting. Update your privacy notice accordingly.
sections.changelog:
1.0.1

  • Improved WordPress.org compatibility, script loading and internal naming.
  • Updated translation-loading compatibility.

1.0.0

  • Consolidated cached-page token refresh and uncached confirmation messages.
  • Restore entered values in the same browser tab after server-side errors.
  • Add localized rate-limit feedback and Unicode-aware length validation.
  • Include 35 frontend language options and five configurable additional fields.
  • Use a time-neutral translated rate-limit message in all supported frontend languages.
  • Improve defensive validation and avoid counting failed mail deliveries against the rate limit.

0.2.3

  • Corrected frontend stylesheet URL generation.
  • Count only structurally valid enquiries toward the rate limit.
  • Aligned server-side field size limits with frontend constraints.
  • Added right-to-left direction support for Hebrew locales.

0.2.2

  • Removed the Ideas and improvements section and non-working email suggestion button from plugin settings.

0.2.0

  • Added Estonian, Arabic, Simplified Chinese and Traditional Chinese frontend language packs.
  • Added shortcode language override and English fallback.
  • Added editable labels, up to three custom fields and text/button hex colours.
  • Added improvement suggestion link to settings.
  • Fixed escaping of the privacy-policy link.

0.1.0

  • Initial development release.
